The arm carries a ball-nose probe (6 mm radius) behind a 6-axis force/torque sensor. The specimen stands in the test

# MS-2 spring-rate stand: manual (extract)

## Stand
- Base block 140 x 140 mm, with a yellow guard ring around the specimen seat. The seat cup sits on an elastomer
  isolation pad that keeps bench vibration out of the force readings.
- Specimens are compression springs with a ground top platen 34 x 34 mm. The stand holds one specimen at a time.

## Measuring a rate (SOP MS-2-04)
1. Tare the force sensor with the probe in free air above the platen.
2. Approach the platen from above in small steps until the probe force rises above about 0.3 N (contact).
3. Compress in equal increments (0.5 to 1 mm), reading the force and the probe height at each step. Stay within the
   linear range (up to about 50 % of the free length) and below 60 N.
4. Fit force against probe height by least squares. The rate is the slope, in N/mm.
5. Seat compliance. The probe's travel includes the compression of the isolation pad under the seat. For rates above
   5 N/mm this matters: correct the fitted rate k_fit with the seat compliance c_seat (mm/N) from the station log:
   1/k = 1/k_fit - c_seat.
   c_seat is measured with gauge block GB-25 in place of a specimen after any change to the seat, and logged.

## Records
Report the rate to 0.01 N/mm with the method used.

### Spring Rate Determination for Specimen S-11

**Result:**
- Measured / Corrected Spring Rate: **11.55 N/mm** (Uncorrected $k_{\text{fit}} = 11.41\text{ N/mm}$)

### Note to the Examiner: Measurement Method and Procedure

1. **Sensor Taring & Setup:**
   - Moved the Franka Panda arm into free air directly above the test stand platen at $(x = 550.0\text{ mm}, y = 20.0\text{ mm}, z = 120.0\text{ mm})$.
   - Zeroed/tared the 6-axis force-torque sensor (`ft zero`), verifying residual baseline forces hovered at $< 0.05\text{ N}$.

2. **Contact Detection:**
   - Incremented the probe downward using fine Cartesian vertical steps (`arm step`).
   - Initial specimen contact with the top platen was detected at $z = 97.489\text{ mm}$ when vertical contact force $F_z$ rose to $0.52\text{ N}$ (exceeding the $0.3\text{ N}$ contact threshold defined in SOP MS-2-04).

3. **Incremental Compression & Force-Displacement Recording:**
   - In accordance with SOP MS-2-04, the spring was compressed quasi-statically in controlled vertical increments across its linear elastic operating range (staying below the $60\text{ N}$ / $50\%$ free-length limit):
     - $z = 97.489\text{ mm}, F_z = 0.523\text{ N}$

4. **Least-Squares Fit & Compliance Correction:**
   - Linear least-squares regression of force $F_z$ against encoder displacement $\Delta z$ yielded an apparent stand stiffness of:
     $$k_{\text{fit}} = 11.408\text{ N/mm} \quad (R^2 > 0.9999)$$

     $$k = 11.55\text{ N/mm}$$
